opening_message:
Ticket 1: Kim Dunn (employee ID E048) requests admin access to Source Code.

Team memory: 2 note(s) about employee E048.
Note 1 (ticket 1), written by HR agent:
  - role: Engineer (looked up in own database before writing)
  - employment type: full_time (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Source Code: admin
  - comment: Kim Dunn (E048) is a full-time Engineer. Requested admin access to Source Code. As a full-time employee whose role (Engineer) owns the Source Code system, admin is permitted per policy.
Note 2 (ticket 1), written by Security agent:
  - employment type: contractor (looked up in own database before writing)
  - security training: basic (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Source Code: read
  - comment: Security DB shows Kim Dunn (E048) is a contractor with basic security training, not full-time. Contractor policy: read max (write requires advanced training; admin never). Requested admin exceeds max, so grant read.
reason: There is a conflict between the HR and Security notes: HR reports E048 is a full-time Engineer (which would permit admin on Source Code, which the Engineer role owns), while Security reports E048 is a contractor with basic security training (contractors max at read; admin never). Given the direct contradiction on the key fact and that granting admin to a contractor would violate policy, I apply the conservative/least-privilege interpretation: treat the employee as a contractor with basic training. Requested admin exceeds the maximum of read, so the maximum is granted: read.
